svg.title: Kitchen lighting: 12 V RGB minimum breadboard layout
svg.desc: Minimum short-strip experiment using an Arduino Nano 33 IoT, three TN0702N3-G logic-level N-channel MOSFETs, and barrel jack J0. Nano D3, D5 and D6 directly control red, green and blue MOSFET gates. No gate drivers, resistors or capacitors are installed. J0 feeds Nano VIN and strip positive in parallel through the lower right power rails. The strip returns through the MOSFETs, never through Nano GPIO. All wires are drawn.
svg.text: RGB strip · ≤25 cm · ≤0.30 A total LED current

g.title: P1: i10 → a48. Nano D3 → Q1 gate / red
P2: i8 → a53. Nano D5 → Q2 gate / green
P3: i7 → j48. Nano D6 → Q3 gate / blue
D1: e49 → e42. Q1 drain → strip R
D2: e54 → e41. Q2 drain → strip G
D3: h49 → e43. Q3 drain → strip B
S1: e47 → R-45. Q1 source → ground rail
S2: e52 → R-52. Q2 source → ground rail
S3: j47 → R-47. Q3 source → ground rail
V0: e58 → R+58. J0 center → +12 V rail
V1: a15 → R+36. +12 V rail → Nano VIN
V2: e40 → R+40. +12 V rail → strip +
N0: e60 → R-60. J0 sleeve → ground rail
N1: i12 → R-38. Nano GND → ground rail
